Cardiovascular disease: factors and prediction

70,000 patient records stored in SQL Server 2019, queried from Python, analysed with statistical tests and classified with machine-learning models. SQL Server and local Jupyter replace IBM Db2 on Cloud and Watson Studio under the lecturer-approved alternative.

70,000patients

1. Key findings

  • Systolic blood pressure (AP_HI), cholesterol and age are the main risk factors — consistently across correlations, hypothesis tests, OLS and the final model's feature importance.
  • The blood-pressure columns contained impossible readings (values in the thousands, negatives, diastolic above systolic). After IQR capping, AP_HI changed from a weak to the strongest predictor.
  • Alcohol intake shows no significant association (p ≈ 0.055). Smoking and activity are statistically significant but with negligible effect sizes.
  • The selected model, tuned Gradient Boosting, reaches 73.4% accuracy, 75.2% precision and 69.6% recall on unseen data, against a 50% baseline.

2. Data and quality

Source: data/cardio_train_raw.csv — 13 columns (ID, 11 features, target CARDIO), age in days. No missing values; all 70,000 IDs are unique; 3,208 rows repeat another row's measurements with a different ID and are kept as distinct patients.

3. SQL storage and queries

The table dbo.CARDIO_TRAIN has a primary key on ID and CHECK constraints on every coded column. Notebook 01 imports the CSV once, verifies every stored row against the source on later runs, runs the 13 queries below through pyodbc, exports the table and re-verifies it after reopening the connection. T-SQL uses TOP n with a full ORDER BY so every row-limited result is deterministic.

With 70,000 observations even tiny differences are significant, so effect sizes are reported alongside p-values. OLS (R² = 0.235) confirms positive, significant effects for AP_HI, AGE, CHOLESTEROL, WEIGHT and AP_LO, and a negative effect for ACTIVE; GENDER is not significant.

7. Classification models

Stratified 70/30 split (49,000 / 21,000, random_state = 42). Each model is a pipeline IQR capping → standard scaling → classifier, so preprocessing never sees test data. The model is chosen by 3-fold cross-validated accuracy on the training set; the test set is used once to report it.

8. Limitations

  • Results describe statistical association in observational data, not causation.
  • SMOKE, ALCO and ACTIVE are self-reported; smokers show a slightly lower disease rate, which reflects confounding (e.g. with gender), not protection.
  • Some implausible values remain after capping (e.g. very low heights/weights), which limits achievable accuracy to about 73–74%.
  • Recall is 69.6%: in a screening setting the decision threshold should be lowered to miss fewer sick patients.
  • For coursework only; not validated for clinical use.
